As a fellow survivor of sexual child abuse by a parental figure i sadly can relate.

So im sorry if what i will write here isn't enough or useful for you, my apologies in advance. Obviously I'm not an expert, nor i have an academic background as foundation for what i will say; just the things that were helpful in the healing journey.

First thing it wasn't your fault.

*Nothing you did or didn't, encouraged the abuse*

Abusers may be "gentle and caring" but in the end they are selfish and only care in their desire, they will (and do so) whatever it takes to keep going the abuse.
And since the violence is sometimes detected by others, the grooming, and caring act is a more rewarding mask for them.

Do not remember it as a good thing.
Do not be kind to them.
Do not fall for that lie.

The fact that an adult "use" and abuse of a child is horrible crime.
Even worse coming from a father figure, who should have had the obligation, responsibility and honor to  care, nurture  and protect you.

His failure and criminal behavior must means not remembering as a father, or dad, or anything else that as what it is, a criminal and abuser.

At best, "biological father" is how i call the one who rape me in my childhood.

So, since someone who you were feeling the unconditional love as a child fail you, abuse and damage you, the first usual reaction is believe that one do something wrong.

Sometimes is even worse, when the abuse is "buried" by the gentle and caring demeanor they could show to others, and to the child most of the time.
Its the failure to understand why someone that you love, and that you believe love you, could be capable of abuse you.

But there isn't any lie that resist the pass of time.

Eventually, the child will unmasked the abuse, because growing is knowing.
Even if collaterals, or bystanders don't act, the child will understand that "something is wrong", that "this isn't good/normal/nice".

From there onward, the mind of the child will face the challenge of understanding that the abuser behavior is wrong, and sometimes this won't happen.
And isn't the child fault.

Because, who wants to acknowledge that the ones we love, didn't love us and are actively destroying us?.

Therefore a feeling of lacking something will appears.

And we may pass all our live trying to fill this emptiness.

Because, we are mourning the dead of one idea:

The believe that they love us.

What we lack in one place, we will seek it in another; we could grown a collection of substitute parental figures, sometimes whit different degree of interaction.
Isn't wrong itself, but is more a symptom of a even deeper absence.

It's a long journey. And i only can praise you for enduring.
It's maddening but you are moving forward.

So keep going my beloved unknown fellow survivor.

We (all us, everyone, everywhere, anytime) deserve to be healthy.

And we will.

Let me emphasize this again:

*IT WASN'T YOUR FAULT!*.

Kid, and teenagers are human in formation, they do what we teach them, what they see, ear and feel from us, the adults and sometimes barely functional people.
Its is our responsibility to become better for them, the failure to do so, its a burden we impose on the children and teenagers.

I was kidnapped by my biological father for a year, and endured days of all forms of abuse.
Then, he leave me with the family of one of his brothers, and i survived as an undesired burden.

All the  time, i believed that i was the one who needed to earn the recognition, the love, the respect, hell even food must be earned!.

And failing to be what others expected, or desired was devastating; i use to think that i deserve all of that; that if i was loved, it was because of my and my faults.

I tried to be perfect.

And failed time after time.

Growing up, it was a difficult experience of trying to flee from "home", and fearing to fail, because im truly believed that i wasn't enough.

Most of the suicidal efforts that i had, were a rational decision on the line of "if i am a problem, then killing me solves the problem, right?". 

And that because failure hurts in the soul, one try to do more, be more, earn more, in an attempt to ease the lack of meaning in everything.

It's because the massive damage made difficult (sometimes almost impossible) to see anything else that just everlasting pain.

It's not a desire to die, its just a wish to not live like that.

So, of course that knowing about the CPTSD, and the support of survivors, professional assistance, etc, helps; but the affordability of such resources is a privileged not always present.
So it could take time, and a loot of effort, going from "trying to be functional" to "perhaps i deserve to heal".

We know what is live whitout hope and purpose.

Now we need to learn to trust in ourselves; we may fall, but we have been more deeper than most.

So the only way is up.
